questions.q: What are Query Store's two internal stores, per this lesson?
options: The plan store (distinct, deduplicated execution plans) and the runtime stats store (aggregated performance metrics per plan, per time interval)
The plan cache and the buffer pool
TempDB and the transaction log
The system health session and the default trace
questions.explain: Query Store separates the plans themselves from their aggregated runtime performance history — that separation is what lets it retain history the plan cache forgets.

questions.q: Why is Query Store more useful than the plan cache for tuning over time, according to this lesson?
options: The plan cache only holds the current plan and forgets everything on recompile or restart, while Query Store retains historical plans and their performance
The plan cache is deprecated in modern SQL Server
Query Store and the plan cache hold identical information
The plan cache cannot be queried with T-SQL
questions.explain: Query Store persists plan and performance history in the user database, surviving events that would silently clear the plan cache.

questions.q: What does setting QUERY_CAPTURE_MODE = AUTO do?
options: Skips capturing infrequent, cheap, ad hoc queries to reduce overhead, while still capturing the queries that matter for tuning
Captures every single query with no filtering
Disables Query Store entirely
Forces every query's plan automatically
questions.explain: AUTO is a middle ground between ALL (capture everything) and NONE (capture nothing new) — it reduces overhead by skipping low-value ad hoc queries.

questions.q: Which catalog view holds the raw SQL text for a query tracked by Query Store?
options: sys.query_store_query_text
sys.query_store_runtime_stats
sys.dm_exec_query_stats
sys.query_store_plan
questions.explain: sys.query_store_query_text holds the SQL text, joined to sys.query_store_query via query_text_id; plan and runtime stats are separate views.

questions.q: What does MAX_STORAGE_SIZE_MB control, and what can happen if it's hit?
options: It caps how much space Query Store can use in the database; hitting it can flip Query Store into read-only mode regardless of the cleanup policy
It caps how many rows a single query can return
It sets the maximum size of the transaction log
It has no real effect and is a legacy option
questions.explain: MAX_STORAGE_SIZE_MB is a hard ceiling; exceeding it can force Query Store to READ_ONLY mode, a production concern covered in Lesson 37.
